page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 64 KB L1d cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 128 MB L3 cache. This server is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is capable of utilizing premium remote storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 25% tier. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive; both large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests, along with the Passmark memory score, rank in the top 10% tier. Database operations also demonstrate top-tier performance, and Redis SET operations achieve strong throughput. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average middle 50% tier. Large-scale LLM inference, specifically prompt processing on a 70B model, represents a performance bottleneck, registering in the bottom 10% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32pls_v6 leverages its ARM architecture to deliver high multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth relative to its resource footprint. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this server as a resource-dense option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory allocations. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores.
